title: Incipient fire detector that ignores dust
space_origin: Brunswick Incipient Fire Detector built for the Space Shuttle orbiters.
earth_use: Discriminates combustion particles from dust, so it gives fewer false alarms; networked sensors provide central fire watch in mines.
psi_note: SAME/SAME-R measured smoke particle sizes and DAFT used the same counter on dust: the data needed to separate smoke from dust.

title: Lightweight firefighter air tanks
space_origin: Developed with NASA Johnson Space Center from spacecraft pressure-vessel technology.
earth_use: 20 lb backpack for 30 minutes of air (13 lb lighter), 4,500 psi composite tanks, better face mask and a personal low-air warning.
psi_note: Background: same composite pressure-vessel know-how used for spacecraft oxygen storage.

title: Fire-resistant firefighter gear (Project FIRES)
space_origin: Lightweight, fire-resistant, heat-protective materials from Apollo suits and spacecraft.
earth_use: New protective ensemble evaluated by 14 municipal fire departments with NASA and FEMA's U.S. Fire Administration.
psi_note: BASS and Saffire burned fabrics such as Nomex: the same class of protective textiles.

title: Fine-water-mist extinguishers
space_origin: Fine-water-mist extinguishers developed for the ISS.
earth_use: Use little water and cause less damage; practical for buildings, ships and data rooms.
psi_note: FLEX quantified how inert suppressants (CO2, He) and dilution raise the oxygen needed to keep burning.

title: Better fire models for buildings and engines
space_origin: Microgravity removes buoyancy and gives simple, model-friendly flames.
earth_use: Validated soot and radiation sub-models improve fire spread prediction on Earth and cleaner combustors (SPICE, CLD Flame, s-Flame).
psi_note: Smoke-point data and soot measurements feed building-fire and engine models.
